summary: This component displays all blog posts that match a specific tag, extracting the tag name from the URL path. It retrieves all blog posts, filters them by the requested tag, sorts them by date with newest first, and renders them as a list of cards. If no tag is specified in the URL or no posts match the tag, it shows an appropriate message.

explanations.9: The regex pattern extracts the tag name from URLs like '/blog/tags/javascript' by capturing everything after '/blog/tags/' and stopping at the next slash or end of string.
explanations.10: decodeURIComponent converts URL-encoded characters (like %20 for spaces) back to their readable form, in case the tag name contains special characters.
explanations.14: useLocation is a hook that gives us the current page's URL information, so we can read what tag the user is looking for from the pathname.
explanations.31: This line collects all unique tag values from every post by flattening the tags arrays and using a Set to remove duplicates.
explanations.32: Since tags might have spaces or special characters that get converted to URL-friendly slugs, this finds the original tag name by comparing slugs, falling back to the raw URL version if no match is found.
explanations.37: The filter checks if any of a post's tags, when converted to a slug, match the slug from the URL—this handles the case where a tag like 'React JS' becomes 'react-js' in the URL.
explanations.38: Posts are sorted by comparing their dates as numbers; subtracting an earlier date from a later date puts newer posts first (descending order).
